fact: Agence Ecofin says Mauritania has been connected to the ACE cable since 2011 and still depends heavily on it, with no fully operational alternative, so ACE outages disrupt internet nationwide; ACE is the single route in service.
The EIB press release says Mauritania connected to the Africa Coast to Europe (ACE) submarine cable in 2010 (other sources say 2011), and that a contract for a second cable was awarded to Ellalink.

EllaLink says it has built a new neutral cable landing station in Nouadhibou that lets Mauritania's national operators access the infrastructure via two diverse routes (landing marked 4 May 2026; the document does not say the branch is yet in service).
DatacenterDynamics reports that only one subsea cable currently lands in Mauritania, the ACE system at Nouakchott, in which International Mauritania Telecom is the Mauritanian participant.
The ACE consortium says the ACE cable was put into service on 15 December 2012 and lists Nouakchott as one of its landing stations, the first international submarine cable to land in Mauritania.
The presentation refers to the existing ACE submarine cable and says the government tendered a second submarine connection landing at Nouadhibou for redundancy, still to start.

Ecofin Agency says the ACE submarine cable has connected Mauritania since 2011 and the country still depends heavily on this single system for international connectivity; a second cable began coastal installation on 4 May 2026 with service expected in January 2027.
Maroc Telecom's nine-month 2025 fact sheet lists, among Moov Mauritel's highlights for January-September 2025, the commissioning of the West Africa submarine cable landing station in Nouadhibou.
system: West Africa submarine cable landing station, Nouadhibou

fact: Moov Mauritel's BU WAC interconnection catalogue for 2025/2026, published on the regulator's site, says it runs the Mauritanian branch of the West Africa Cable submarine cable landing at the Nouadhibou terminal station, with capacity and IP transit sold to Marseille, Lisbon, Seville and Madrid.

The same catalogue, issued after ARE's non-objection under authorisation 221/2024/ARE/CNR/DTTP of 23 December 2024, offers dedicated capacity and IP transit on the WAC cable at published tariffs to Mauritanian operators, internet service providers and international clients.
